verses.text_sanskrit: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते
verses.transliteration: klaibyam ma sma gamah partha naitat tvayy upapadyate
verses.text_english: Do not give in to this faint-heartedness; it does not suit you. Shake off this small weakness of heart and stand up.
verses.commentary: Krishna's first response to Arjuna's collapse: he names the paralysis rather than the enemy.

verses.transliteration: asocyan anvasocas tvam prajna-vadams ca bhasase
verses.text_english: You grieve for what does not deserve grief, though you speak words of wisdom. The wise mourn neither the living nor the dead.
verses.commentary: Grief is addressed directly, as a misreading of what is permanent.

verses.text_english: Contacts with the senses bring cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and they go; they do not last. Learn to bear them steadily.
verses.commentary: The classic verse for equanimity under fluctuating circumstance.

verses.transliteration: karmany evadhikaras te ma phalesu kadacana
verses.text_english: Your right is to the work itself, never to its fruits. Do not let the fruit be your motive, and do not withdraw from the work either.
verses.commentary: Nishkama karma: the anchor verse for performance anxiety and outcome obsession.

verses.text_english: Dwelling on objects breeds attachment to them; from attachment desire is born, and from thwarted desire, anger.
verses.commentary: A causal chain from rumination to anger; useful for anger-management guidance.

verses.transliteration: vihaya kaman yah sarvan pumams carati nihsprhah
verses.text_english: One who moves through life having let go of craving, without the sense of ownership and without conceit, reaches peace.
verses.commentary: The stated end-state of the practice: shanti, not achievement.

verses.text_english: It is better to do your own work imperfectly than another person's work well. To follow a borrowed path is a kind of loss, even when it succeeds.
verses.commentary: The svadharma verse: career comparison, imitation, and borrowed ambition.

verses.text_english: Lift yourself by your own effort; do not let yourself sink. You are your own friend, and you can be your own adversary.
verses.commentary: Self-compassion framed as agency rather than sentiment.

verses.transliteration: bandhur atmatmanas tasya yenatmaiva atmana jitah
verses.text_english: For the one who has mastered the self, the self is a friend; for the one who has not, the self behaves like an enemy.
verses.commentary: Pairs with 6.5 as a two-verse unit on inner conflict.

verses.transliteration: yasman nodvijate loko lokan nodvijate ca yah
verses.text_english: The one whom the world does not agitate, and who does not agitate the world, who is free of elation, resentment, fear and anxiety, is dear to me.
verses.commentary: Describes the temperament sought in the presence of hostile environments.

verses.transliteration: sarva-dharman parityajya mam ekam saranam vraja
verses.text_english: Set aside every other obligation and take refuge in me alone; I will carry you beyond your wrongs. Do not grieve.
verses.commentary: The verse of surrender, offered after all the reasoning has been given.

verses.text_english: Restraint of the senses, which begins with renouncing anger, greed, vanity and rashness, is achieved by cultivating discipline in the sciences one has learned.
verses.commentary: Kautilya makes self-control a professional competence, not a private virtue.

verses.text_english: Appoint as counsellor one who is of good family, capable, trained in the arts, far-sighted, wise, of firm memory, bold, eloquent, energetic, and free of malice and fickleness.
verses.commentary: The hiring rubric of the Arthashastra; used for team-building and delegation questions.

verses.text_english: The ruler should divide the day and the night into equal parts and assign each part its work, for when the ruler is energetic the servants follow; when slack, they too grow slack and consume the work.
verses.commentary: Time-blocking, roughly two millennia early; used for burnout and workload questions.

verses.text_english: Superintendents should be appointed with regard to their work and place, and audited often; officers who handle wealth should be examined by many, for power without accounting turns into appropriation.
verses.commentary: The audit principle: trust is structured, not assumed.

verses.text_english: The six measures of policy are peace, war, staying quiet, marching, seeking shelter, and duplicity of counsel; the wise apply whichever the situation admits, not whichever the mood prefers.
verses.commentary: Shadgunya: a decision framework for conflict, negotiation and strategic waiting.
